result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/design/REQ-031-schema.md, closing the schema dependency docs/agents/design/REQ-031.md Sec0 named and deferred to this role (the REQ-014/016/019 convention for a bot requirement that adds/alters stored data). Read REQ-031.md in full first to derive the exact shape determineNextFeedbackField (Sec2.2) and determineFeedbackFlowStep (Sec2.7) need from the schema, then apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts's current registrations/users tables and REQ-019's five existing profiles skip-tracking columns and REQ-014's consent_pd_at/consent_pd_version pairing as this role's own precedent for column-naming, nullability-justification, migration-prose, and S11/S13 reasoning style, then decisions/0005-orm-drizzle.md for the Drizzle-generated-migration convention (confirmed apps/bot/drizzle/meta/_journal.json's latest entry is 0005_violet_venom.sql, idx 5 -- this migration will generate as 0006_<name>.sql) and security-invariants.md S11/S13 for the redaction/anonymization gates.

Two schema changes designed:

1. NEW feedback table: id (uuid PK), registration_id (uuid NOT NULL, FK -> registrations.id ON DELETE restrict, UNIQUE index -- uq_feedback_registration_id -- the entire mechanism behind AC2's 'a second row fails on a database constraint, verified by a raw duplicate INSERT'), nps (integer NOT NULL, CHECK nps >= 0 AND nps <= 10, named chk_feedback_nps_range, mirroring the existing chk_registrations_checked_in_only_if_admitted convention -- NOT NULL is what makes 'skipping NPS saves nothing' a schema fact, not just an application rule, since writeFeedbackNps is the only INSERT path and always supplies nps), liked/improve (nullable text, no format rule), topic_votes (text[], nullable -- see decision below), liked_skipped/improve_skipped/topic_votes_skipped (three booleans, NOT NULL DEFAULT false), created_at/updated_at (timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()). Confirmed no FK/constraint on this table requires anything to exist before the first insert beyond the registrations row itself -- the row is created on the NPS answer only, per REQ-031.md Sec1.3, and this table's own shape does not force an earlier or placeholder insert.

topic_votes DECISION: text[] (native Postgres array), NOT jsonb -- REQ-031.md Sec0.2 left this genuinely open and named both options. Reasoned explicitly (REQ-031-schema.md Sec1.4): the stored value is already exactly 'an array of strings with no per-item metadata' (parseTopicVotes produces string[], FeedbackRecord.topicVotes is typed string[] | null) -- jsonb here would hold nothing but a bare JSON array, an unneeded serialization layer. events.agenda and audit_log.payload earn jsonb because they hold typed objects or genuinely polymorphic content; topic_votes has neither property. text[] is directly exportable/absorbable with zero JSON-decoding step and directly queryable with unnest() if a future requirement ever needs per-topic counts. Cost stated honestly: this is the first native array column in this schema -- weighed against jsonb's unneeded serialize/parse step for a value that is only ever a flat array of strings, the array's directness wins.

Skip markers: three plain booleans (liked_skipped/improve_skipped/topic_votes_skipped), NOT NULL DEFAULT false, following the REQ-019-schema.md five-booleans-over-one-array precedent exactly, re-derived (not merely cited) for this table: the set is fixed and closed at three (named directly by FeedbackField's own union), matches this schema's own one-boolean-per-fact convention (is_student, publish_consent, blocked, broadcast_opt_in, REQ-019's own five), exportable/absorbable with zero decoding, matches FeedbackRecord's one-property-per-column shape. NOT NULL DEFAULT false for the same two-valued-fact reasoning REQ-014-schema.md Sec1/REQ-019-schema.md Sec3.2 already applied -- writeFeedbackNps's INSERT supplies no explicit value for any of the three, so DEFAULT false fills them for free on row creation.

2. NEW users.broadcast_opt_in_asked_at: nullable timestamptz, no default -- resolves REQ-031.md Sec0.3 exactly as that document already specified (nothing further was open on it). Confirmed it mirrors consent_pd_at/consent_pd_version's existing pairing convention (REQ-014-schema.md Sec10) precisely: nullable, no default, both-or-neither NOT enforced by a schema constraint (that discipline lives in writeBroadcastOptInAnswer, REQ-031.md Sec2.6, the design's own stated single write site for both columns) -- the identical declination REQ-014-schema.md Sec10 made for its own pair, for the identical reason (no acceptance criterion asks the DB to reject an unpaired state, and a single write site is a stronger practical guarantee than a CHECK would add).

Migration: Drizzle-generated per decisions/0005 (BACKEND-DEV runs drizzle-kit generate against an updated schema.ts, never hand-written) -- one CREATE TABLE feedback (with its FK, UNIQUE index, and CHECK constraint) plus one ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN broadcast_opt_in_asked_at, expected as the next sequential 0006_<generated-name>.sql. No backfill needed for either (CREATE TABLE is empty; ADD COLUMN with no default sets every existing users row to NULL, which is exactly the correct 'never asked' state for a pre-existing row). Reversibility stated honestly: DROP TABLE feedback is a clean structural reversal but destroys real respondent answers if any exist by rollback time (flagged as an operational, not schema-level, concern); dropping broadcast_opt_in_asked_at is lossy in the same narrower sense REQ-014-schema.md Sec11 already accepted for consent_pd_version (the 'already asked' fact is lost, broadcast_opt_in's own answer survives). Neither down-migration fails outright the way re-imposing NOT NULL can (REQ-019-schema.md Sec5.1) -- both are mechanically safe to run at any time.

S11: no phone/email column added; liked/improve/topic_votes are free text that could incidentally carry identity-adjacent content a respondent chose to type, but REQ-031.md's own design never echoes their content into a log/audit payload/third-party message. S13: nps should survive a future anonymization routine (aggregate-shaped, like show-rate); liked/improve/topic_votes are flagged as an open question for a routine that does not yet exist in this codebase to decide, not resolved by invention here (same restraint REQ-019-schema.md Sec6 exercised for its own not-yet-built-routine case). feedback.registration_id FK is ON DELETE restrict, matching every existing FK in this schema -- confirmed this introduces no exception to the established default, since no requirement in scope hard-deletes a registrations row.

Added a one-line 'Resolved' cross-reference in docs/agents/design/REQ-031.md's own Sec0 pointing to the new schema doc and confirming FeedbackRecord's shape matches column-for-column -- no other edit to CODE-DESIGNER's design.

issues.description: docs/agents/design/REQ-031-schema.md Sec8 open question 1: whether feedback.liked/improve/topic_votes should be included in a future S13 anonymization routine's blanked-field list. No such routine exists yet in this codebase to extend, so this is left as a decision for whichever future requirement implements S13's routine, not resolved here. nps is reasoned to clearly survive (aggregate-shaped); the three free-text columns are the open part.

docs/agents/design/REQ-031-schema.md Sec8 open question 2: no CHECK constrains topic_votes's array length or element content. Declined since parseTopicVotes already drops empty segments before any write and no acceptance criterion caps topic count -- flagged in case SECURITY-REVIEWER/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR wants a defensive bound anyway, same restraint class as REQ-019-schema.md Sec3.4.

docs/agents/design/REQ-031-schema.md Sec8 open question 3: no CHECK forbids a feedback value column being non-null while its matching *_skipped flag is true, for the identical reason and with the identical caveat REQ-019-schema.md Sec3.4/Sec10 open question 1 already recorded for profiles' five columns -- restated here rather than silently assumed for feedback's three.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 1b) -- both docs/agents/design/REQ-031.md and REQ-031-schema.md ready for gating together, per REQ-031.md Sec0's own stated blocker now closed.
